authority: CTO Round 200 directive: execute Level 3 §103/KSR attack for R199-C4 per NOVELTY_FIRST_DISCOVERY_ENGINE_V1 (Round 160).
constitutional_basis: Article II — exact evidence beats semantic plausibility
Article VII — never weaken the verifier to rescue a claim
Article XIX — never optimize for the gate
Article XXVIII — no silent semantic promotion
Article XXIX — separate implementation failure from mechanism failure
Article XXXVII — Future-Novelty Test (ratified this round)

the_candidate.name: R199-C4 Self-Identifying Therapeutic System
the_candidate.the_invention: A therapeutic system that continuously determines WHETHER its internal model of the patient is still valid. Five-step architecture: (1) PREDICT response to intervention, (2) OBSERVE actual response, (3) COMPARE, (4) DECLARE MODEL FAILURE (discrete event), (5) AUTOMATICALLY re-identify patient + SWITCH to SAFE FALLBACK policy.

the_strongest_103_ksr_combinations.combination_logic: US 12,636,471 provides the closed-loop implanted shunt platform. Industrial mismatch detection provides the predict-observe-compare mechanism. OGSRL provides the OOD guardian (abstain on out-of-distribution). A PHOSITA could combine these.
the_strongest_103_ksr_combinations.does_it_teach_all_five_steps: PARTIAL — teaches predict/observe/compare and abstain. Does NOT teach DISCRETE model-failure DECLARATION (vs continuous uncertainty), AUTOMATIC re-identification (vs clinician-triggered), or SAFE POLICY SWITCHING (vs mere abstention).
the_strongest_103_ksr_combinations.what_is_missing: Steps 4 (declare discrete failure) and 5 (auto-reidentify + safe switch). OGSRL abstains but does not re-identify or switch policy.

the_strongest_103_ksr_combinations.combination_logic: iLet provides continuous patient-specific model learning. OGSRL provides OOD detection. PCCP provides regulatory motivation for model drift detection.
the_strongest_103_ksr_combinations.does_it_teach_all_five_steps: PARTIAL — teaches continuous learning + OOD detection. Does NOT teach DISCRETE failure declaration (iLet keeps learning, never declares failure) or SAFE POLICY SWITCHING (OGSRL abstains, does not switch to fallback).
the_strongest_103_ksr_combinations.what_is_missing: The DISCRETE declaration step (iLet is continuous, not discrete) and the SAFE POLICY SWITCH (OGSRL abstains, does not switch to a known-safe fallback).

the_strongest_103_ksr_combinations.combination_logic: VIEshunt provides safe learning-based control of shunt. Industrial mismatch provides detection. Safe RL provides abstention.
the_strongest_103_ksr_combinations.does_it_teach_all_five_steps: PARTIAL — VIEshunt is a vision paper, not an issued patent. Does not claim the full five-step architecture.
the_strongest_103_ksr_combinations.what_is_missing: The full integrated architecture is not claimed. VIEshunt focuses on safe exploration, not model-failure-triggered re-identification.

the_strongest_103_ksr_combinations.combination_logic: US 12,636,471 provides the shunt. BrainSense provides adaptive control. Industrial mismatch provides detection. PCLC provides fault-handling guidance.
the_strongest_103_ksr_combinations.does_it_teach_all_five_steps: PARTIAL — teaches adaptive control + fault handling. Does NOT teach DISCRETE model-failure declaration + AUTO-reidentification + SAFE POLICY SWITCH.
the_strongest_103_ksr_combinations.what_is_missing: BrainSense keeps adjusting within envelope (continuous, not discrete). PCLC is generic fault handling (open-loop fallback), not model-failure-aware re-identification.

aspect_1_discrete_failure_declaration.description: R199-C4 declares model failure as a DISCRETE EVENT (boolean flag), not a continuous drift score. iLet and BrainSense use continuous learning — they never 'declare' failure.
aspect_1_discrete_failure_declaration.rationale: No prior art teaches DISCRETE model-failure declaration in an implanted medical device. Industrial mismatch detection uses continuous scores. Safe RL uses continuous uncertainty. The discrete declaration is a design choice that enables the subsequent re-identification step.

aspect_2_automatic_reidentification.description: R199-C4 AUTOMATICALLY (device-initiated) re-identifies the patient model after declaring failure. No clinician trigger required.
aspect_2_automatic_reidentification.rationale: No prior art teaches automatic device-initiated patient re-identification. iLet does continuous updating (not re-identification from scratch). FDA PCCP contemplates pre-planned modifications (not real-time automatic re-identification). This is genuinely non-obvious.

aspect_3_safe_policy_switching.description: R199-C4 SWITCHES to a SAFE FALLBACK CONTROL POLICY during re-identification. Not mere abstention (H6/OGSRL) or freeze — an active safe policy.
aspect_3_safe_policy_switching.rationale: No prior art teaches switching to a safe fallback CONTROL POLICY during re-identification. OGSRL abstains (no policy). PCLC uses open-loop fallback (generic, not model-failure-aware). The safe policy switching is genuinely non-obvious.

the_h6_overlap_analysis.rationale: H6 (Uncertainty-Gated Autonomous Intervention Twin, Round 198) and R199-C4 are conceptually adjacent but architecturally distinct. H6 = pre-action uncertainty quantification (intervene / observe / abstain). R199-C4 = post-action model validation (declare failure / re-identify / safe switch). A system implementing H6 would naturally evolve toward R199-C4 as the next step after sustained high uncertainty. The two are COMPLEMENTARY, not independent.
the_h6_overlap_analysis.the_distinction: H6 governs ENTRY into an intervention (should I act?). R199-C4 governs EXIT + RECOVERY when the intervention reveals the model was wrong (my prediction failed; re-identify the patient; switch to safe policy).
the_h6_overlap_analysis.mitigation: If both survive their killer experiments, they may both be promoted. But the promotion dossiers must explicitly state: H6 covers pre-action uncertainty gating; R199-C4 covers post-action model failure + re-identification + safe switching. No double-counting of the 'uncertainty' concept. The patent claims must be drafted to cover non-overlapping architectures.

what_the_competitor_would_need_to_discov: The architectural insight that model failure should be a DISCRETE EVENT (not continuous drift).
The design for AUTOMATIC device-initiated re-identification (vs clinician-triggered or continuous updating).
The SAFE FALLBACK POLICY bank and switching logic (vs mere abstention).
Regulatory approval for automatic re-identification without clinician oversight (FDA PCCP may not cover this).
the_2028_competitor_build_scenario.the_competitor_build_timeline: A 2028 competitor would need 2-3 years to discover and validate the architecture, then 2-3 years for regulatory approval (automatic re-identification is harder than PCCP). Earliest commercial availability: 2030-2033.
the_2028_competitor_build_scenario.the_competitor_build_difficulty: HIGH — the components exist in separate fields, but the integrated architecture and its regulatory path are not established.

future_novelty_test_verdict.rationale: The components exist in 2026 in SEPARATE fields (industrial control, safe RL, medical devices). The integrated architecture (discrete declaration + auto-reidentification + safe switching in an implanted device) requires a NEW ARCHITECTURAL INSIGHT that is NOT in the 2026 literature. A 2028 competitor would need to discover this architecture and navigate a harder regulatory path. This meets the Article XXXVII standard.
future_novelty_test_verdict.the_new_scientific_insight_required: The ARCHITECTURAL INSIGHT that model failure should be a DISCRETE EVENT triggering automatic re-identification and safe policy switching, rather than continuous gradual updating (iLet) or mere abstention (H6/safe RL).

the_killer_experiment_summary.the_experiment: Intentionally introduce an unmodeled physiological transition. If the controller continues optimizing confidently instead of recognizing model failure, kill it.

post_level_3_novelty_assessment.rationale: R199-C4 CONFIRMS novelty level 3. All three non-obvious aspects (discrete declaration, automatic re-identification, safe policy switching) survive the §103 attack — none is taught by any combination of prior art. The Future-Novelty Test PASSES: a 2028 competitor would need to discover the architectural insight and navigate a harder regulatory path. NOT upgraded to level 4 (WORLD_CLASS_CANDIDATE) because: (a) the killer experiment has not yet confirmed the architecture works; (b) buyer/moat analysis has not been completed; (c) the H6 overlap creates a MODERATE double-counting risk that must be resolved before promotion. The candidate remains at level 3, simulation-eligible, with the killer experiment as the next decisive test.

honest_disclosure.what_this_attack_does: Constructs the strongest §103/KSR combinations and tests whether they teach all five steps of R199-C4's architecture.
honest_disclosure.what_this_attack_does_NOT_do: Cannot confirm the architecture WORKS — that requires the killer experiment (Round 201). Cannot resolve the H6 overlap — that requires comparing killer experiment results.
honest_disclosure.limitations: The H6 overlap is MODERATE. If H6's killer experiment (future) shows that uncertainty-gated abstention already covers most of the value, R199-C4's incremental value may be smaller than expected.
honest_disclosure.caveats: The architectural novelty is harder to defend against §103 than component novelty. The killer experiment is the strongest defense — if run and published, it provides concrete evidence that commercial adaptive controllers (iLet, BrainSense) FAIL the model-failure recognition test, while R199-C4 PASSES.
